translation_notes: Three `"PREFIX ns: <...> SELECT ..."` strings passed to g.query become s{ } islands; the three PREFIX lines become one `@prefix ns:` at the head of the function. The islands are kept in q_fields / q_matches / q_ms and handed to g.query (rdflib returns ResultRow, so r.id, r.wdDistrito... are unchanged). All three have OPTIONAL or are used with r.<var> access, hence s{ } rather than m{ }.

The two Wikidata templates (dq, sq) stay strings: they hold the placeholder {{VALUES}}, are sent as text to query.wikidata.org by get_wikidata_info and are not queries on a graph of the program (they are not valid SPARQL before the substitution).

Context shim preprocess_shim.py: get_wikidata_info of the source, verbatim; and the module-level paths, moved out of original.py because the source derives them from __file__ and would read/write outside the example directory: KG_PATH is fixture.ttl (N-Triples, parsed with format='nt' as the region does) and DATA_DIR the example directory (CSV files are compared as text by the harness and removed). The network is replaced in the driver by a local stand-in for requests.get (ok / HTTP 500 / raises).

Fixture: fields with and without sameAs (one with two), a field without coorY, a non-Campo with a field's properties, matches with a dateTime and with a date, a match without resultado2, a match outside any competition, a broken competition chain. Observed: stdout and the two CSV files. A mutant dropping the resultado2 pattern of q_matches fails the check (verified).
optimization_notes: Both sides: the three query variables (q_fields, q_matches, q_ms) and the two Wikidata templates (dq, sq) are inlined into their calls; the four `.map(lambda x: info.get(x, {}).get(key) if pd.notna(x) else None)` lines share a nested helper `wikidata_column(uris, info, key)`, with the pd.notna guard kept; the local query texts are compacted with `;` only.

Blank nodes `[ ns:nombreEquipo ?local ]` in place of the named join variables ?el/?ev were tried and dropped: on a 200-match graph rdflib then returns the rows in another order, and the row order of matches.csv is observable. A `;` that keeps the same triples in the same order does not change it (checked).

optimized.ldpy: s{ } for the three queries (q_fields and q_ms have an OPTIONAL; q_matches is a basic graph pattern, but m{ } returns its rows in another order on the same 200-match graph, so s{ } stays); the PREFIX of each string becomes one `@prefix ns:` in the function.
Exception to the symmetry rule, island-only: `@graph as g` replaces `g = Graph()`, and the s{ } islands are iterated on that current graph without a `(g)` suffix.
Notation ratio above 1: the three queries are one string token each in Python and are counted token by token in s{ }.
header_optimization_notes: Python: nothing unused in the header; copy of optimized.py.
